exposure: COVID-19 infection in late stages of pregnancy
cohort: The study included 168 pregnant women infected with COVID-19 in the late stages of pregnancy, of whom 86 had abnormal liver function and 82 had normal liver function.
finding: Abnormal liver function tests in pregnant women with late-stage COVID-19 are associated with an increased risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, with maternal age, gestational week, and BMI being independent risk factors for liver injury.
mod_finding: The cesarean section rate was significantly higher in pregnant women with abnormal LFTs following COVID-19 infection.
cross-section timing: Data were collected from December 2022 to January 2023.
